newsitem.title: UK: Guinness /GrandMet see deal this year.
newsitem.headline: Guinness /GrandMet see deal this year.

text.p: Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan Plc said on Friday they expected their proposed merger to become effective two or three months after the end of October following news the European Commission had started a full probe into the deal.

"As foreshadowed, Grand Metropolitan and Guinness have been informed by the European Commission that it will require additional time to complete its investigations," the companies said in a joint statement.
"The European Commission's decision is expected by the end of October and the proposed merger is expected to become effective two or three months later," they said.
The planned merger would create a company -- to be called GMG Brands -- worth more than 20 billion pounds which would be the world leader in wine and spirits.

It would bring together an empire stretching from Johnnie Walker and Bell's whisky, Gordon's Gin, Smirnoff Vodka, and Guinness' traditional stout to the Burger King fast food chain, Haagen Dazs ice-cream and Green Giant canned vegetables.
The plan is, however, opposed by Bernard Arnault, the chairman of LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton, which has a 14.2 percent stake in Guinness.

In two share raids he has snapped up a 6.29 percent stake in GrandMet and spent around 800 million pounds in an effort to leverage a better negotiating position for his plan to create a pure drinks company with LVMH's Moet & Chandon and Hennessy brands, without the GrandMet Burger King and other foods businesses and Guinness brewing interests, analysts said on Friday.
LVMH is now the largest shareholder in both the would-be merger partners.
U.S. competition authorities have also asked for secondary information on the proposed Guinness/GrandMet merger.
